prompt: What makes an event an incident rather than a ticket?
hint: The last words of the definition.

choices.text: Users are hurt and the response needs coordinating
It happened at night, outside the team's working hours
choices.why: Time of day does not define it.

choices.text: Its cause is unknown
More than one alert fired within the same five minutes
How hard the fix looks
choices.why: That is not the users' view.

choices.text: Which service failed
choices.why: The same service can fail in small and large ways.

choices.text: The impact on users
How senior the person on call is

prompt: You are unsure whether a problem is SEV-2 or SEV-3. What does the lesson advise?

choices.text: Pick the lower one to avoid waking people who may not be needed
Wait until the cause is known, so that the severity is right
choices.why: Waiting is the habit that hurts.

choices.text: Ask the customers
Pick the higher one and lower it later if needed

prompt: Match each role to what it does.
Why should the incident commander not debug?

choices.text: Commanders are usually not engineers
Someone outside the problem has to notice what nobody is doing
Debugging is slower when it is done by one person on a shared screen
Commanders do not have production access in most companies, by policy

prompt: What is the phrase "I am going to…, objections?" for?

choices.text: To ask permission from management before touching production
choices.why: It is addressed to the responders.

choices.text: To start the timeline
So that two changes to production never collide
To hand over command

prompt: The page arrives. Which question does the lesson ask first, and why?

choices.text: What changed? Recent changes are the likeliest cause, and reversible
Who wrote the code? To call them
Is the database up? It is always the database
How much has the budget burnt? To decide the postmortem

prompt: Why roll back before understanding the bug?

choices.text: Rollbacks always fix the root cause
choices.why: They remove the change, not the cause.

choices.text: The bug cannot be studied after a rollback, since its logs leave with the release
A rollback ends the incident by definition, whatever the numbers then say
Customers are failing now; understanding waits, a rollback does not

prompt: After the rollback the burn rate is still high for a minute or two. What is the most likely reading?

choices.text: The rollback failed and must be repeated before anything else is tried
The windows still hold failures from before the rollback
The cause was something else
Prometheus has stopped scraping the storefront since the rollback restarted it

prompt: Which belongs in an incident update?

choices.text: When the next update will come
The name of the engineer who made the release
A guess at the root cause, to reassure people
The PromQL behind the alert
choices.why: Not for the readers of updates.

prompt: There is nothing new fifteen minutes after the last update. What should be sent?

choices.text: Nothing until there is news
A detailed technical log of everything tried
An update saying no change, and when the next one is
A request for ideas from the whole company

prompt: Why build the timeline from annotations and the pager's log rather than from memory?

choices.text: Memory is not allowed in a postmortem
Annotations are more detailed than people, since they record every command typed
The pager deletes its log after a day
The marks were written at the moment, with exact times

prompt: In the lab's timeline, how many marks did people write during the incident: the release, the declaration, the rollback and the resolution?

choices.text: When the root cause is understood
When users are no longer affected and the system is stable
When the postmortem is written
When the commander goes off shift and hands the incident to the next person

prompt: Why write the follow-ups down before the channel goes quiet?

choices.text: They must be approved by the incident commander that night
The tickets system closes at midnight
By the next morning nobody remembers half of them
They are needed to lower the severity

prompt: Three engineers each restart a different service during an incident, and the error rate drops. Nobody knows which restart helped. What role was missing?

choices.text: A commander deciding one change at a time, and a scribe recording it
A second operations lead
A communications lead
choices.why: Updates would not have sorted the changes.

choices.text: Nobody: the incident is over, so it does not matter

prompt: Put the steps of the lab's incident response in order.
items: Read the page and the burn rates
Ask what changed and find the release mark
Wait for the page to resolve and mark the end
